identity.description: Netlify is a web hosting and deployment platform (sites, atomic deploys, serverless functions, forms, DNS). Its public REST API at api.netlify.com manages sites and deploys, per the docs.
identity.identity_notes: The docs.netlify.com API reference and developers.netlify.com guides describe the Netlify platform and its REST API. This matches the named app.

auth.oauth_flows: An OAuth app is registered under User Settings > Applications > New OAuth app. The developer guide's example authorization URL uses response_type=token, which is the implicit flow. Other grants (e.g. authorization code) are not established.
auth.token_refresh: Not established. The guide only says PATs 'offer configurable lifespans'; the example sets expires_in to 604800 (7 days).
auth.scopes_notes: Scopes not established from sources reviewed.

access.production_restrictions: No app-review requirement found for public integrations. SAML/SSO teams deny personal access tokens to the team by default, and access must be granted when the token is generated. Admin approval is therefore possible for SSO teams, but it is not a general gate.

api.rate_limits: 500 requests per minute for most requests. Deploys are limited to 3 per minute and 100 per day. Responses include X-RateLimit-* headers.
api.limitations: Endpoint paths other than GET /sites come from third-party listings and were not checked against the official spec. The OpenAPI definition is Open API 2.0 and still described as a work in progress. The support forum warns that endpoints missing from the OpenAPI reference may change.
